title: ARISE Plant DNA Extraction
author: Kevin Beentjes
materials: Tissue Sampling Note: For high throughput, DNA extraction can be performed in plates rather than individual tubes. Within ARISE plant tissues are processed in Qiagen Collection Microtubes (Qiagen cat no. 19560) plates, which fit into a TissueLyser using plate adapters. Place up to 0.5 cm 2 of silica dried leaf tissue into a plate of collection microtubes or 1.5 ml eppendorf tubes. Tissues other than leaf may work with unverified success rates. Optional: Grind tissue with a tube pestle, tweezers or cut the tissue with a scalpel. Make sure the tissue is broken up into smaller pieces to allow efficient maceration. Add three sterile 2mm glass beads per sample.

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Buffer A
steps.instruction: Make 100 mL of Lysis Buffer A by adding 13.4 mL of 1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 8) to 50 mL Milli‑Q water, then 10.6 mL of 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8); stir until dissolved, adjust pH to 9.0 with NaOH, and bring the final volume to 100 mL with Milli‑Q.

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Buffer B
steps.instruction: Make 100 mL of Lysis Buffer B by dissolving 3.4 g guanidine thiocyanate, 17.4 g trisodium phosphate dodecahydrate, and 0.4 g NaCl in 50 mL Milli‑Q water on a heated magnetic stirrer; adjust pH to 9.0 with HCl and bring to 100 mL with Milli‑Q.

steps.title: Prepare Tissue Lysis Additive
steps.instruction: Prepare 100 mL of 15 % Tween 20 solution by mixing 15 mL Tween 20 with 85 mL Milli‑Q water; stir gently without creating bubbles.

steps.title: Prepare Tissue Binding Buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 26.3 g guanidine hydrochloride in 20 mL Milli‑Q water, bring the volume to 50 mL, then add 50 mL 100 % ethanol to obtain 100 mL Tissue Binding Buffer.

steps.title: Prepare Elution Buffer
steps.instruction: Make 100 mL of Elution Buffer by adding 1 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 8) to 75 mL Milli‑Q water, then 0.2 mL 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8); bring to 100 mL with Milli‑Q and vortex briefly.

steps.title: Dissolve Salt Crystals if Needed
steps.instruction: If salts in Lysis Buffer B or Tissue Binding Buffer crystallize, heat the affected buffer at approximately 55 °C for 10 minutes (or until fully dissolved).

steps.title: Assemble Sample Lysis Mix
steps.instruction: For each sample add 50 µL Lysis Buffer A, 50 µL Lysis Buffer B, 7.7 µL Tissue Lysis Additive (15 % Tween), and 5 µL RNase A (12 mg/mL); mix with a TissueLyser for 30 seconds at 30 Hz, then centrifuge 2 minutes at maximum speed to collect the lysate.

steps.title: Activate RNase A
steps.instruction: Incubate the lysed samples at 37 °C, 400 RPM for 30 minutes on a shaking incubator to activate RNase A.

steps.title: Overnight Lysis Incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the samples at 55 °C, 400 RPM overnight on a shaking incubator; after incubation store samples at 4 °C or stop the protocol.

steps.title: Bind DNA to Magnetic Beads
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the incubated lysates for 15 minutes at maximum speed at room temperature to pellet solids; transfer 75 µL supernatant to a deep‑well plate, add 20 µL SeraSil‑Mag 400 beads (pre‑shaken), add 150 µL Tissue Binding Buffer (2× lysate volume), and incubate 15 minutes at room temperature on a shaker.

steps.title: Wash Magnetic Beads
steps.instruction: Place the plate on a magnetic rack, discard supernatant, then:

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL isopropanol, shake at 500 RPM for 2 minutes at room temperature; settle on magnet and discard supernatant.
Add 400 µL 96 % ethanol, shake at 500 RPM for 2 minutes; settle and discard supernatant.
Repeat the 400 µL ethanol wash once more.
Remove all residual ethanol and dry beads for 5–10 minutes at room temperature (or 50 °C).

steps.title: Elute DNA
steps.instruction: Add 50–70 µL Elution Buffer (or Milli‑Q) to each bead sample, shake at 500 RPM for at least 5 minutes, settle beads on the magnet, and transfer the supernatant containing DNA to a new plate or tube.

steps.title: Calibrate Tissue Binding Buffer pH
steps.instruction: Prepare a 5 mL lysis mixture: 2.17 mL Lysis Buffer A, 2.17 mL Lysis Buffer B, 330 µL Milli‑Q, and 330 µL 15 % Tween; add 10 mL Tissue Binding Buffer to this mixture in a 50 mL tube, adjust to pH 4.0–4.5 with 5 M HCl (≈350 µL for the 10 mL calibration), record the HCl volume, and scale proportionally for larger volumes (e.g., 3.5 mL HCl for 100 mL Tissue Binding Buffer). Verify pH by mixing 10 mL binding buffer with 5 mL fresh lysis mixture and measuring; repeat verification whenever a new Lysis Buffer B is prepared.

steps.title: Optional Physical Lysis
steps.instruction: Freeze the tube or plate ends in liquid nitrogen for a few seconds, repeat until the contents are solid, then process with a TissueLyser for 150 seconds at 30 Hz and centrifuge 15 minutes at maximum speed.
